results.snippet: The salary range for this role is $5,000 - $9,500 per month (Gross in USD) About Sezzle : With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping! Compensation : For this principal development role, with 6+ years of experience, the compensation range is $5,000 - $9,500 USD per month, based on experience level and gross amount. This range acknowledges the extensive expertise, leadership capabilities, and significant contributions expected at this level, offering a competitive salary to reflect the value of advanced skills and experience About the Role: We are seeking a hands-on, high-impact Senior Security Engineer, Detection & Response , to strengthen security operations at Sezzle : detection, incident response, and vulnerability management across our cloud infrastructure and applications. You will join the team that runs our SIEM and detection capability — from log ingestion and audit coverage to detection rules, alert tuning, and investigation workflows — so that access to sensitive systems is attributable and suspicious activity is caught and attributed by our own detections. You will operate the vulnerability-management loop end-to-end, and when incidents happen, you will lead the investigation and see the long-term fix through. You should consider yourself a DOer - someone who is comfortable diving into logs, analyzing systems, validating findings, and working end-to-end to get issues resolved. You will report to the Director of Information Security and work alongside the engineers who own the security platform and network and zero trust — your detection and response work is what proves their controls hold. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment and wants to work on real-world security problems at scale. At Sezzle , AI-assisted engineering is a standard part of how we work. In this role you will use and build agentic workflows for alert triage, investigation, and threat hunting that multiply what the team can cover. You are excited to use automation and emerging technologies (including AI) to take repetitive security work off the team's plate
You balance strong security standards with business needs and can support privacy and compliance requirements in a practical, scalable way

To explore how our suite of solutions is shaping the future of customer success, check out the link https://www.gainsight.com. About This Role: We’re looking for a full-time Staff Security Operations Engineer to join our Security team reporting to the Senior Manager, AI Response & Threat. This role is a hybrid role based out of our Hyderabad, India or Bangalore, India. Deep familiarity with attacker tactics and techniques (MITRE ATT&CK) and how to translate them into detection logic - Excellent communication skills, with the ability to brief executives and technical teams alike during incidents and planning discussions Nice-to-have skills or experience: - Hands-on experience with cloud-native detection and posture tools (e.g., AWS GuardDuty, Azure Sentinel, Wiz, Prisma Cloud) - Familiarity with container and orchestration security (Docker, Kubernetes) and associated attack surfaces - Experience with threat intelligence platforms and proactive threat hunting using frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK or Sigma rules - Exposure to purple team or adversary simulation exercises (e.g., Atomic Red Team, Caldera) to validate detection coverage - Relevant certifications (e.g., GCIH, GCFA, GCTI, CISSP, OSCP) - Working knowledge of network security architecture, including segmentation, zero trust principles, and cloud network security groups - Experience with vulnerability management programs, including scanning, prioritization, and remediation tracking - results.description: About the Role: Grade Level (for internal use): 11 The Team The Cyber Fusion Center protects the business by combining threat intelligence, monitoring, detection engineering, incident response, and security automation into one proactive, intelligence-led defense capability. By breaking down silos, the team reduces risk and strengthens security across the enterprise. The team prioritizes collaboration, continuous learning, and innovation, with shared ownership of outcomes and a supportive learning mindset during high-pressure situations. This is a hands-on, build-driven environment where team members work with real-world use cases, rapidly develop new capabilities, and continuously improve the organization’s ability to detect, investigate, and respond to emerging threats. Responsibilities and Impact Design, develop, test, and maintain high-quality detections for threats including malware, ransomware, identity attacks, insider threats, cloud threats, network, AI, and advanced persistent threats. Develop detection logic across SIEM, EDR/XDR, cloud, network, identity, and application security platforms using tools such as Splunk SPL, Microsoft Sentinel KQL, Elastic Query DSL, Sigma, and YARA. Apply artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data science techniques to identify anomalous behavior, emerging threats, attack patterns, and indicators of compromise. Build and maintain security analytics and data pipelines using Python, SQL, Pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, and Databricks. Conduct threat hunting and hypothesis-driven investigations to identify gaps in existing detection coverage. Map detections to the MITRE ATT&CK framework and improve coverage of priority attack techniques. Analyze false positives, false negatives, alert quality, and detection performance, implementing improvements based on measurable results. Collaborate with SOC, Incident Response, Threat Intelligence, SOAR, Cloud Security, and Vulnerability Management teams to develop effective detection capabilities. Implement detection-as-code practices using version control, peer review, automated testing, CI/CD, documentation, and controlled deployment. results.snippet: About Centric Software: Centric Software® is a global leader, providing an innovative and AI-enabled product-concept-to-commercialization platform for retailers, brands and manufacturers of all sizes. We equip retail, fashion, luxury, footwear, outdoor, home and consumer goods brands with pioneering best-of-breed solutions to plan, design, develop, source, comply, buy, make, price, allocate, sell and replenish products. Our technology powers brands to streamline processes, drive efficiency and operate with confidence in an ever-changing market. Our story is one of rapid growth, bold ideas and extraordinary opportunities. We’re here to challenge the status quo—and we’re looking for brilliant people who want to do the same. No matter where you are in the world, this is your chance to be part of something exceptional. Job Description 1.1    SIEM G SOAR Engineering (Palo Alto Cortex) Design, deploy and maintain log source integrations into Palo Alto Cortex XSIAM / XSOAR, ensuring normalisation, parsing accuracy and data quality across all connected sources. Develop, test and continuously improve SOAR playbooks for automated triage, enrichment and response across key incident types. Own SIEM content including detection rules, correlation policies, dashboards and alert thresholds; perform ongoing tuning to reduce false-positive volumes. Maintain platform health including connector status monitoring, API rate-limit management and capacity planning for log ingestion pipelines. Produce and maintain engineering documentation including integration runbooks, playbook specifications and change records in accordance with CAB policy. 1.2    Endpoint Security Engineering (CrowdStrike Falcon) Administer and engineer the CrowdStrike Falcon platform, including sensor deployment management, policy configuration and response workflow alignment with SOC procedures. Configure and maintain Falcon data connectors into the SIEM, ensuring EDR telemetry is enriched and actionable within the detection pipeline. Contribute to host-based detection content and work with the SOC team to validate alert fidelity from Falcon- sourced events. Support incident response activities requiring Falcon RTR (Real Time Response) capabilities where required. 1.3    Cloud Security Logging G Integration Engineer and maintain security log collection from multi-cloud environments into the SIEM, including: ◦    AWS — configure and operate GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and S3 access logging; manage event forwarding via EventBridge and SǪS/SNS pipelines. ◦    Azure — configure and maintain Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Azure Monitor Diagnostic Settings and Entra ID audit and sign-in log ingestion. ◦    GCP — configure and maintain Cloud Audit Logs, Security Command Centre findings export and Pub/Sub-based log forwarding into the SIEM. Ensure cloud logging coverage aligns with the organisation’s detection requirements and regulatory obligations, and identify and remediate gaps in telemetry coverage. Maintain cloud-side IAM roles and service principals used for log collection with least-privilege principles. 1.4    Microsoft Entra ID G Office 365 Integration Work alongside the IT team to maintain and improve security-relevant integrations between Entra ID and the SIEM, including Conditional Access policy audit logging, risky sign-in alerting and identity-based detection use cases. Support the health and configuration of Microsoft 365 Defender connectors, including Exchange Online, SharePoint and Teams audit log ingestion. Cybersecurity Analyst Location: Remote – Anywhere in India Work Schedule: Monday to Friday Work Arrangement: Fully Remote Experience: 5-8 Years Job Summary We are seeking an Information Security Analyst with 3–5 years of experience across security operations, vulnerability management, and governance, risk, and compliance (GRC). The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience with security monitoring tools, incident response, and security frameworks such as SOC 2 Type II and NIST CSF. This is a fully remote opportunity open to candidates based anywhere in India, with a Monday-to-Friday work schedule. The role involves strengthening the organization's security posture, supporting compliance initiatives, identifying and mitigating security risks, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to implement effective security practices. Key Responsibilities 1. Security Operations & Tooling Monitor, tune, and triage security alerts across SIEM platforms, escalating confirmed incidents in accordance with established procedures and runbooks. Manage the vulnerability management lifecycle, including scanning, risk-based prioritization, remediation tracking, and management reporting. Support endpoint security, email security, and network monitoring tools, identifying security gaps and recommending configuration improvements. Scripting or automation experience using Python or PowerShell for security tooling, analysis, and reporting. Exposure to cloud security environments, including AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Experience with GRC platforms such as Archer, ServiceNow GRC, Drata, or Vanta. We empower you with the ability to predict, prescribe, and automate smarter, more profitable business decisions to improve operating margins. Why join Coupa? Pioneering Technology: At Coupa, we're at the forefront of innovation, leveraging the latest technology to empower our customers with greater efficiency and visibility in their spend. Collaborative Culture: We value collaboration and teamwork, and our culture is driven by transparency, openness, and a shared commitment to excellence. Global Impact: Join a company where your work has a global, measurable impact on our clients, the business, and each other. Learn more on Life at Coupa blog and hear from our employees about their experiences working at Coupa. The Impact of a Lead Security Engineer at Coupa: Coupa's Security Engineering team protects our enterprise, product, platform, and customer data at scale. As Lead Security Engineer, you will be a hands-on technical leader on the Security Engineering team — architecting and building cloud security controls, setting engineering standards, and partnering closely with Engineering, IT, and Compliance to ship durable, automated security tooling rather than one-off fixes. You thrive on ambiguity, sweat the implementation details, and take pride in solutions that scale across hundreds of accounts and services. What You’ll Do Architect and build multi cloud security controls across Coupa's cloud environment. VPC segmentation, security groups/NACLs, IAM policy design using least-privilege and permission boundaries, and Organizations/SCPs for guardrails at scale. Build policy-as-code and IaC security guardrails and wire them into CI/CD as pre-merge and pre-deploy gates rather than after the fact reviews. Harden containerized workloads - image scanning, admission control, pod security standards, and runtime detection. Write auto-remediation for cloud misconfiguration and drift so common findings close without manual ticket routing. Own Vulnerability management program, act as the technical escalation point for security incidents and vulnerability findings - leading forensics, containment, and root-cause analysis using cloud-native and EDR tooling, and driving remediation to closure. Partner with Risk & Compliance to translate audit framework requirements (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP) into concrete technical controls, and automate evidence collection by integrating cloud telemetry with GRC tooling. Mentor other security engineers through design review, threat modeling, and code/architecture review; raise the technical bar for the whole team. Own reference architectures, threat models, and runbooks for the security tooling you build; participate in and help improve the on-call rotation. What You Will Bring to Coupa 10+ years of security engineering experience, including significant hands-on work securing production cloud environments at scale, plus experience leading projects or mentoring other engineers. Deep, hands-on AWS security expertise - IAM, VPC/networking, KMS, GuardDuty, Security Hub, Config, and Organizations/SCPs; working knowledge of GCP or Azure security is a plus. Production experience with Terraform (or equivalent IaC) and policy-as-code frameworks, plus container/Kubernetes security tooling. Strong software engineering fundamentals - Python and/or Go, Git-based workflows, and building/maintaining CI/CD security integrations (SAST, DAST, SCA). Experience with SIEM/SOAR platforms and vulnerability management tooling (e.g., Wiz, Qualys, Tenable) - building detections and workflows, not just consuming dashboards. Working knowledge of compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP, NIST 800-53) sufficient to translate control requirements into engineering work. Excellent written and verbal communication skills - able to write clear technical design docs and explain risk trade-offs to auditors and engineering leadership alike. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Relevant certifications a plus: CISSP, CCSP, CISA, or AWS/GCP security certifications. Some international travel may be required. The successful candidate’s starting salary will be

Our technology is relied upon by major security-forward companies around the globe and we are consistently rated as the #1 trusted low-code security automation platform. Our mission is to prevent breaches and enable continuous compliance via a low-code security automation platform that serves as the system of record for the entire security organization.Get an understanding of Swimlane here: What’s the best thing about working at Swimlane? If you ask the team, they'll tell you it's the people. Swimlaners are innovative, collaborative and driven by the purpose of revolutionizing the way security teams automate and respond to alerts. Headquartered in beautiful Louisville, Colorado, directly between Denver and Boulder, Swimlane's staff spans 16 countries! Senior Security Solutions Engineer Reports to: Content Engineering Manager The role We are hiring a senior builder to design, ship, and sustain security solutions and reusable components on Swimlane Turbine, published to the Swimlane Marketplace. This is not a platform-engineering role and not a pre-sales role. You will turn real SOC and managed-service workflows into productized automation: playbooks, components, case experiences, and dashboards that any enterprise or MSSP can install, configure, and run.  The people who do this well have already lived the problem — building security workflows inside a large-enterprise SOC or an MSP/MSSP, then encoding that judgment into automation others can trust. What you will own Solutions — end-to-end Turbine packages for high-value use cases (SIEM/EDR alert triage, phishing, vulnerability operations, identity response, threat intel, case management). Components — reusable ingestion and enrichment building blocks with clean interfaces, so playbooks compose instead of being rewritten per vendor. .  Marketplace quality — versioned, documented, tested content that deploys cleanly across tenants. What you will do Translate SOC and MSP operating models into Turbine playbooks, components, apps, and dashboards that are customer-agnostic and configurable. Normalize vendor-specific data into common schemas (OCSF / TEDS and Turbine interfaces) using native actions, JavaScript, and Python. . Design workflows that mix deterministic automation with AI-assisted steps — enrichment, summarization, classification — with explicit human-in-the-loop controls. . Integrate across the security stack via connectors and APIs: SIEM, EDR/XDR, identity, threat intel, ticketing, and cloud security tools. Package, version, and publish Solutions and Components to the Marketplace; own docs, test cases, and release notes. Partner with Product, UX, Platform, QA, Sales Engineering, and Professional Services to turn field demand into content that scales. Raise the bar on content quality: reuse, testability, failure handling, and operability at enterprise and multi-tenant scale. What you bring 7+ years in software development, solutions architecture, or security automation — with hands-on time building SOC or IR workflows, not only writing code next to a security team. Direct experience in a large-enterprise SOC or an MSP / MSSP, including triage, investigation, enrichment, escalation, and response. Proficiency in Python and JavaScript, JSON/API integrations, and transforming messy third-party payloads into reliable schemas. Hands-on work on at least one SOAR or security automation platform: Swimlane, Cortex XSOAR, Splunk SOAR, Tines, Torq, or equivalent. Working knowledge of SIEM and EDR/XDR (for example Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, CrowdStrike, Defender, SentinelOne) and how analysts actually use them. Comfort with ambiguity: you can take an incomplete use case, define the workflow, and ship a maintainable solution. Clear written and verbal communication with both engineers and security operators. Nice to have Prior Swimlane Turbine, Marketplace, or content-pack experience. OCSF or similar normalization work; MITRE ATT&CK fluency. Building or tuning AI agents / LLM-assisted SOC workflows, including guardrails and confirmation steps. Multi-tenant or MSSP service-delivery design. HTML/CSS or widget work for analyst-facing layouts and dashboards. Security certifications (GCIH, GCIA, CISSP) or SOAR platform certifications. What this is not Not a sales-engineer quota role. results.snippet: The salary range for this role is $5,000 - $9,500 per month (Gross in USD) About Sezzle : With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping! Compensation : For this principal development role, with 6+ years of experience, the compensation range is $5,000 - $9,500 USD per month, based on experience level and gross amount. This range acknowledges the extensive expertise, leadership capabilities, and significant contributions expected at this level, offering a competitive salary to reflect the value of advanced skills and experience About the Role: We are seeking a hands-on Senior Security Engineer, Network & Zero Trust , to own the network pillar of Sezzle 's zero-trust program: every connection explicitly allowed, authenticated by service identity, and attributable after the fact — across our Kubernetes clusters, AWS accounts, and the paths between them. You will take ownership of our network-policy program — default-deny micro-segmentation across our Kubernetes clusters — and carry the rest of the pillar forward with it: identity-aware service-to-service transport, per-application private access, flow-level visibility, and network configuration managed as reviewed code. This is an engineering role: you will write the policies, the tooling, and the rollout automation yourself, and you will carry changes through other teams' services without breaking delivery. You will report to the Director of Information Security and work alongside the engineers who own the security platform and detection and response, and with the platform and IAM teams on service identity — your network controls are what their work relies on, and your telemetry is what their detections run on. At Sezzle , AI-assisted engineering is a standard part of how we work. In this role you will use and build agentic workflows — flow analysis, policy generation from observed traffic, drift review — that let the team segment a large estate. What You’ll Do: Own east-west segmentation across our Kubernetes clusters: design the segmentation model, derive network policies from observed traffic, and keep every workload reachable only through explicitly allowed, identity-bound paths — a default that holds as the estate grows, not a one-time project. Deliver identity-aware transport — design and roll out mutually authenticated, encrypted service-to-service connections (mTLS), so that authorization decisions rest on verified service identity. Keep a live map of the network: VPC peerings, tunnels, cross-account links, and every public entry point — built from cloud APIs and reconciled continuously, so every path into production is known and justified. Own segmentation of production and the cardholder-data environment: implement and enforce the CDE and high-trust-tier boundaries, review every peering and public exposure against them, and run segmentation testing with the security team. Partner with IT on private access: evaluate and help deliver per-application access (ZTNA) for engineers and operators reaching production systems. Own network telemetry: flow logs east-west and north-south, with enough identity on both ends that "who talked to what, when" is answerable in minutes — and feed it to our SIEM for the detection team. Own cluster admission control and hold the line on drift: workload admission policy (pod security, image provenance, network policy), security groups and firewall rules declared in git, applied only through the IaC pipeline, with admission control at the gate and drift detected and reverted automatically. Contain: build the levers that let us isolate a workload or segment quickly when detection flags lateral movement, and take part in incident response when

Contain: build the levers that let us isolate a workload or segment quickly when detection flags lateral movement, and take part in incident response when the network is in play.
Participate in threat modeling and design reviews for anything that changes how traffic flows, and in the on-call rotation for the controls you own.
6+ years of experience in security, network, platform, or infrastructure engineering, with hands-on ownership of network controls in cloud production environments.
Deep, practical Kubernetes networking knowledge: CNI, NetworkPolicy semantics, DNS, ingress/egress — and experience rolling segmentation out on live clusters without outages.
Strong AWS networking: VPCs, subnets, security groups, peering and Transit Gateway, PrivateLink, load balancers, flow logs.
Hands-on experience with mTLS and service-to-service authentication (service mesh, proxies, or CNI-level encryption).
Infrastructure as code as your default way of working — Terraform and Helm or equivalents, through merge requests and CI, across repositories you don't own.
Ability to write real code (Go, Python, or Bash) for tooling and automation, not only configuration.
Ability to investigate directly with packet captures, flow logs, and system-level data.
Working knowledge of PCI DSS network requirements — segmentation, scoping of the cardholder-data environment, segmentation testing.

Demonstrated AI-forward engineering: you actively use AI tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or custom LLM integrations) in your work today and have opinions grounded in practice about where it helps and where it doesn't.
Cilium / eBPF in production, including Hubble or equivalent flow observability.
mTLS at fleet scale, including certificate lifecycle — service mesh (e.g., Istio, Linkerd, Cilium service mesh) and workload identity standards such as SPIFFE/SPIRE.
You have built AI-assisted workflows that others adopted — flow analysis, policy generation, drift review.
Experience evaluating or deploying ZTNA / identity-aware proxy products. ● Policy-as-code and admission control (OPA/Gatekeeper, Kyverno, conftest).
Experience with network detection — IDS/IPS, anomalous-flow and lateral-movement detection — and with containment during incidents.
Familiarity with SOC 2 and with FFIEC-style examination expectations for network security. ● Experience in fintech, payments, BNPL, or other regulated environments.
You'd rather close a path than document it - an allow-list that exists in production beats a diagram of how the network should look.
You change other teams' systems without breaking them - you roll out in observe mode first, measure, and earn the right to enforce.

You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed.
You’re not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things
You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking.
You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.

You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly.
You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle.

Backend: Golang
Database: MySQL, Postgres, Elasticsearch
DevOps & Cloud: AWS, Kubernetes
Version Control: Git
CI/CD: Gitlab
Testing: Developer and AI-driven, focus on automated end-to-end, integration, and unit tests

results.snippet: About the role You’ll be the engineer our managed services clients rely on when something looks wrong in their AWS accounts or on their endpoints, and the one who makes sure it doesn’t happen twice.You will run AWS-native security services and enterprise EDR/XDR platforms across many client environments, lead incident response from the first alert to the root cause, manage devices through Microsoft Intune, and keep the controls and evidence clients need for SOC 2. The stack you’ll own: Five layers, many client environments. These are the services and tools you’ll work with every week. AWS foundation Accounts, identity, encryption and network edges AWS Organizations & SCPs Control Tower IAM & IAM Identity Center IAM Access Analyzer KMS Secrets Manager VPC & Network Firewall AWS WAF & Shield Cloud workloads EC2, containers and serverless, protected by AWS-native and thirdparty tools CrowdStrike Falcon Cloud Security Trend Micro Vision One / Cloud One Workload Security Bitdefender GravityZone Amazon Inspector GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring Systems Manager Patch Manager ECR image scanning Amazon EKS Endpoints, mobile and email Laptops, servers, phones and the mailboxes people use on them CrowdStrike Falcon SentinelOne Singularity Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Bitdefender GravityZone Microsoft Intune Intune app protection (MAM) Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access Microsoft Defender for Office 365 SPF, DKIM & DMARC Detection and response EDR, XDR and MDR working as one service Amazon GuardDuty AWS Security Hub Amazon Detective AWS Security Incident Response Microsoft Sentinel Microsoft Defender XDR MDR partners Compliance and evidence Proof that controls work, ready for auditors SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria AWS Config conformance packs AWS Audit Manager AWS CloudTrail CIS Benchmarks Key responsibilities: AWS cloud security Design and run a multi-account security architecture for each client: a dedicated security tooling account with delegated administration for GuardDuty, Security Hub, Inspector, Macie and Detective, and an organization-wide CloudTrail delivered to a locked-down log archive account. Enable and tune GuardDuty protection plans (S3, EKS, Runtime Monitoring, Malware Protection, RDS and Lambda), maintain suppression rules, and route findings by severity to the right queue and on-call engineer. nClouds : Cloud Security Engineer Page 2 of 7 Operate Security Hub with central configuration across the organization: enable standards (AWS Foundational Security Best Practices, CIS, PCI DSS and NIST SP800-53), build automation rules and custom insights, and keep findings deduplicated. Own identity security: IAM Identity Center permission sets, service control and resource control policies, permission boundaries, cross-account role trust reviews, root account protection, MFA enforcement, access key rotation, and IAM Access Analyzer findings for external and unused access. Protect data with KMS key policies and rotation, S3 Block Public Access and bucket policy reviews, default EBS and RDS encryption, Secrets Manager rotation and Macie sensitive data discovery. Harden networks through security group and NACL reviews, AWS Network Firewall, Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall, VPC endpoints, WAF managed and rate-based rules, Shield Advanced and VPC Flow Log analysis. Secure containers and serverless: EKS cluster hardening, EKS Pod Identity or IRSA, Kubernetes RBAC and audit logs, ECR enhanced scanning, and least-privilege Lambda execution roles. Build auto-remediation for common risks, such as public S3 buckets, security groups open to the internet on SSH or RDP, disabled logging and exposed access keys, using AWS Config rules, EventBridge, Lambda and Systems Manager Automation. Centralize security logs (CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS, WAF and load balancer logs) in Amazon Security Lake or the client’s SIEM, with retention set to meet compliance needs. Run security posture reviews against the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark, AWS Foundational Security Best Practices and the Well-Architected Security pillar, then drive remediation with the client. Review Terraform and CloudFormation changes for security misconfigurations before they reach production.
